attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, asserted in his own voice. The others he mentions (the 'thousands of people') are only the target of his claim, not its source.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the claim's scope: the concerns he raised in 2022 (reliability, understanding of the world, hallucination) and 'not even close'. It is a retrospective observation, not a forecast. Dropping the aside about his interlocutors is appropriate.

contract.note: The plain reading is that substantial practical limitations persisted despite development, and that one remaining error is not enough. That is an ordinary, fair reading of 'not even close'. The result still depends on that reading, because the phrase sets no threshold.

evidence.note: November 2025 benchmark, published before the post. GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Grok-4 and others hallucinate above 10% on grounded summarisation. The new dataset is harder, so it does not show any trend over time.

OpenAI's own disclosure (September 2025): GPT-5 hallucinates significantly less but still does, and it calls hallucination a fundamental challenge. The admitted improvement tempers but does not defeat the claim.
PhyX (May 2025): GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 and o4-mini score 32–46% on physical reasoning, far below human experts. Earlier than the late-2025 frontier, but inside the target period.

SimpleToM (October 2024): frontier models including o1-preview do poorly on applied theory-of-mind questions. Targeted prompting helps, but the authors call that a fragile workaround. Earlier generation, inside the target period.

reviews.rationale: Dated evidence from the target period shows substantial recurring failures in all three areas: GPT-5-era hallucination above 10% (e1) and admitted by OpenAI (e2), weak physical reasoning (e3), and poor applied theory of mind (e4). That meets the support condition. Real progress (e2, and the prompting gains in e4) and the older models in e3 and e4 limit precision, but they do not show dependable performance.
